column10: Unsoundness is deliberate and documented

column10: First-hand maintainer testimony; matches PEP 484 rationale

column10: MSR'22; confounds acknowledged; any usage correlated with worse metrics

column2: Python needed roughly a decade to settle annotation semantics: PEP 563 (2017; defer evaluation) was superseded by PEP 649/749 and annotations still run at import time by default
column10: PEP 563 notes hints evaluated at import time are not computationally free

column2: Go released in 2009 without generics for simplicity and the Go 1.18 release (2022) added type parameters constrained by interfaces after the team judged the design worth its complexity
column10: FAQ: polymorphism did not seem essential at the time

column2: The generics delay reflects the generic dilemma: a language must choose between slow programmers; slow compilers and bloated binaries; or slow execution times with no free option
column10: Cox (2009) + Go FAQ agree but share the Go origin; hence medium

column2: Go deliberately omitted exceptions and type inheritance arguing try-catch coupling produces convoluted code and inheritance forces manual type-relationship bookkeeping
column10: FAQ sections on exceptions and inheritance

column2: V8 replaced Full-codegen/Crankshaft with an interpreter-plus-optimizing-compiler pipeline (Ignition+TurboFan; v5.9; 2017) because the old compiler could not keep pace with JS language evolution

column10: Overview frames per-tool repetition as the problem

column2: Go's module system uses minimal version selection and a go.sum file of checksums to authenticate downloaded module content

column2: Lua ships as a small core with I/O; string; math and OS functions in external libraries and embeds via a C API as host-controlled extension language with no main program
